root.title: Does longer warmup keep big runs stable?
root.description:
About one run in five past 1B parameters diverges in its first few thousand steps. Each Belief under this Issue is one explanation, and each Experiment is evidence for or against one of them.

**Done when** one explanation holds on three seeds at 1.3B and the others are ruled out.

belief.title: A 2k-step warmup prevents early divergence at 1.3B
belief.description:
In the warmup sweep, no run with 2,000 or more warmup steps diverged, while runs with 500 diverged on 3 of 10 seeds. Two reruns at a larger batch disagree, which is why the confidence is not higher.

- Holds at 350M and 1.3B.
- Not yet tried at 7B.

words: cosine decay beats linear past 20k steps
seeding every sampler removes the drift
the rank cache keeps token ids identical

cost._note: What a seed charges each record, in USD, on the two axes the ledger keeps: agent (the LLM spend of whoever or whatever ran the step) and resource (the compute it triggered). A kind missing here is written at zero and gets no cost write at all. That is deliberate for Issue and Belief, and it is the honest story as much as the cheap one: a claim and the question it answers cost nothing to state, and testing them is where the money goes, so the spend belongs on the runs and sessions that did the work, not on the record holding the verdict. Nor is it free to leave them charged: a cost write is a marginal_cost change, which alerts each dependent one hop, and the roots of the big islands fan out to a thread's whole width at once. The ranges are an ML research lab's. An Experiment is GPU-hours, so its resource cost dwarfs everything and its agent cost is the few dollars of watching it. An AgentSession is the opposite: tokens, little compute. A CodeChange sits between, a rerun of something and the writing of it. An Artifact is a render and a page. Paper, WebResult and WebSearch are near free -- a download, a parse, one search call -- so their ranges are pennies, kept above zero so the row reads as spent-something, which it did. Every axis of a priced kind stays above zero, so each carries a cost on both. Each value is picked from its range by a hash of the title, as the summary is, so two seeds write the same number.
